recent_commits.message: Add Tier-1 extension rules for GIS, phylogenetics, mass spec, and 3D scan data
recent_commits.body:
data_classify_files() had no format-locked rule for ESRI Shapefile
components, GeoPackage, phylogenetic tree formats, mass spectrometry
data, 3D scan data, or generic tabular text, so recognition depended
entirely on folder/filename-keyword fallback. A file with no such hint
(e.g. sitting at an archive's root) fell through to "unknown" even
when the extension alone is unambiguous evidence of research data.

Added .shp/.dbf/.shx/.prj/.sbn/.sbx/.cpg/.gpkg, .nex/.nwk/.tre/.phy,
.mzxml/.mztab, .ply, and .tab/.table as Tier-1 data extensions, and
wired .tab/.table into data_read_head()'s delimited-text reader so the
readable=TRUE flag has a matching parser. .stl is deliberately left
alone (stays "materials"), since it conventionally names a
3D-printable model rather than scan data, unlike .ply.

Fixes #441

recent_commits.message: Fix repo_check misses for 4TU, Dataverse, Figshare, DSpace7, and DataONE
recent_commits.body:
4TU (#431): .researchdata4tu_id() extracted a DOI-embedded uuid and passed
it straight to v2/articles/<id>, but the API needs a different numeric id
only a live DOI redirect reveals. Added .researchdata4tu_resolve_uuid() to
follow that redirect before querying.

Dataverse (#432): .dataverse_host_from_doi() returned the first host sharing
an ambiguous DOI prefix, picking the wrong DANS Data Station for a shared
prefix (10.17026, used by 4 separate installations). Now resolves via live
DOI redirect when a prefix maps to more than one host; also added the
missing phys-techsciences.datastations.nl prefix entry.

Figshare (#434): added collection-URL/DOI detection
(.figshare_collection_id()/.figshare_collection_articles()), mirroring the
existing project-expansion pattern. Share-links remain correctly flagged as
unsupported (no public API resolves them).

DSpace7/DataONE (#435): dataone_links() missed KNB's real #view/doi: URL
shape and had no fallback for a bare legacy KNB docid (knb.1404.1) cited
with no DOI at all. dspace7_links() had no DOI-based detection whatsoever,
so a paper citing only a DOI (never the host string) was invisible to it --
added live DOI resolution against known DSpace7 hosts.

#433 needed no change: 10.6078 was already added to
.dryad_doi_prefixes() by an earlier commit, before the issue was filed.

All fixes verified live against each issue's reported example. No
regressions in existing archive-dataone/dataverse/dryad/figshare tests.

recent_commits.message: Widen archive-member byte-range retry beyond the fixed 403/429/5xx list (#429)
recent_commits.body:
.http_range_bytes() -- the call .zip_member_fetch() makes for both a
member's local header and its compressed data -- only retried a response
matching .storage_is_transient()'s fixed list (403, 429, 500, 502, 503,
504). Any other status (a plain 401, a 400, or anything else not on that
list) was accepted as final after exactly one try, even when the identical
request succeeded moments later on manual reproduction: nothing
distinguishes "this host will never honour ranges" from "that one request
happened to fail" for an unlisted status.

.range_status_is_transient() now retries anything except 200 (host is
deliberately ignoring Range -- a fixed property of the host/URL a retry
cannot change) and 206 (success). Verified against a real, unmocked local
HTTP server that returns 401 once then 206 -- httr2's own retry loop
(req_perform1 -> retry_is_transient(), independent of req_error()'s is_error
override) correctly retries and succeeds on the second attempt.

httr2::local_mocked_responses()/with_mocked_responses() do not exercise
req_retry()'s actual retry loop at all (mock responses return through
handle_resp() before the while(tries < max_tries) loop is reached) -- a
limitation already independently documented elsewhere in this codebase
(test-repo-download.R's skipped "skip_on_api_limit = TRUE gives up on a
confirmed rate limit fast" test). Tests here check the request's configured
retry policy directly instead of trying to simulate multiple attempts
through a mock.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: Record archive-member download failures in download_repo_files() itself (#429)
recent_commits.body:
The previous commit fixed error propagation inside .zip_fetch_members()/
.zip_member_fetch(), but missed the actual call site the issue reported:
download_repo_files()'s archive-member block (R/repo-download.R) wraps
.zip_fetch_members() in tryCatch(..., error = function(e) NULL) and, on
any failure -- a thrown error, or a listing that returns NULL, or an
individual member coming back ok = FALSE -- just does `next`, leaving
file_location = NA with nothing recorded anywhere. This is the exact code
quoted in the issue.

Moved `failed`'s initialization earlier (it previously appeared after this
block ran, so there was nowhere to record into) and now populate it for
all three failure shapes, matching the has_url path's existing convention:
the roll-up message() and attr(files, "failed") already downstream pick
these up unchanged.

recent_commits.message: Record why a zip archive-member fetch failed instead of a silent NULL (#429)
recent_commits.body:
.zip_fetch_members()/.zip_member_fetch() collapsed every failure -- a
transient range-request error, a corrupt local header, a CRC mismatch, a
path-traversal rejection, a write failure -- into an indistinguishable
ok = FALSE with no message anywhere, so a corpus-scale run had no way to
tell a retryable failure apart from a host that will never support this.
Each failure path now records a one-line reason, and the five per-provider
download functions (Dryad, Zenodo, Figshare, Dataverse, ReShare) surface it
as a progress message and attach it as a `failed` attribute on the returned
table, matching the convention download_repo_files() already uses.

recent_commits.message: Persist zip_peek() to disk and thread skip_on_api_limit through it (#427)
recent_commits.body:
zip_peek()'s result was cached only in memory (.zip_peek_cache), reset every
R process, unlike repo_info_cache() which already persists a repository's
LISTING to disk for exactly this reason. Added an on-disk cache
(R/zip-peek-cache.R, mirroring repo-info-cache.R's shape: one file per
archive URL, opt-in via cache = TRUE) and wired it into zip_peek(),
zip_decision(), .zip_fetch_members(), and .code_expand_zip(), plus all of
their call sites in repo_check.R, data_check.R, code_check.R, and
repo-download.R.

Also fixed skip_on_api_limit not reaching zip_peek()'s own HTTP helpers:
.head_size(), .http_range_get(), .http_range_tail(), .http_range_suffix(),
.http_range_bytes(), and .range_size() all called .wait_out_known_rate_limit()
and the retry factories with no skip_on_api_limit argument, so a confirmed
exhausted rate limit was always waited out during a zip peek regardless of
what the caller asked for -- the argument only reached them via the global
metacheck.skip_on_api_limit option. repo_check() had no skip_on_api_limit
parameter at all; added one, and data_check()/code_check() now forward their
own skip_on_api_limit both to repo_check() (via module_run()) and to the
zip-peeking step, matching how they already forward cache the same way.

recent_commits.message: Merge pull request #426 from scienceverse/fix-424-zip-peek-s3
recent_commits.body: Fix zip listing on S3-backed hosts, install-loop variables as packages, empty code files
recent_commits.author: Daniel Lakens

recent_commits.message: Fix zip listing on S3-backed hosts (#424), install-loop variables as packages (#421), empty code files (#425)
recent_commits.body:
#424: zip_peek() on Dryad, Figshare and Harvard Dataverse
- These hosts redirect downloads to Amazon S3, which refuses HEAD (403)
  but honours ranged GETs. When HEAD gives no size, the tail is now
  requested by distance from the end ("bytes=-n") and the total read
  from Content-Range; a 416 answer is handled. The fallback reads the
  status before any body and accepts only 206, so a host that ignores
  the range cannot send a whole archive.
- A size is taken from HEAD only when the answer is 2xx; a 403 on a
  size request is no longer retried.
- .remote_size() falls back to a one-byte ranged GET the same way.
- Removed the OSF, Zenodo and Dataverse whole-archive routes in
  download_repo_files(): those archives never report a size, so the
  routes never ran. Removed .remote_content_length().
- Dryad, GitHub and GitLab archives now follow one rule: size estimated
  from listed file sizes, skipped when unknown or above 2x
  max_download_size, and stopped during download at 2x. GitHub and
  GitLab previously had no limit.
- osf_file_download(mode = "zip"): max_download_size is a budget for the
  whole project. A node whose archive does not fit is downloaded file by
  file within the budget (previously reported as "not downloaded" and
  then downloaded without limit). Partial archives are deleted.
- peek_zips now defaults to TRUE in data_check and reproducibility_check.

#421: dependency extraction
- code_library_names() no longer reports a variable's name as a package
  in install.packages(), requireNamespace(), or library()/require() with
  character.only = TRUE. Variables are resolved to the literal names
  assigned in the file (including for-loop variables, lapply(pkgs,
  library), p_load(char = pkgs)), and dropped otherwise.
- A package install.packages() cannot find is reported with its "not
  available" warning instead of "installed but not loadable".
- A 404 from the CRAN Archive is reported as "not found in the CRAN
  Archive", not as a network failure.

#425: empty code files
- code_abs_path(), code_setwd(), code_install_packages() and
  code_line_stats() handle an empty file without warnings or errors;
  code_parse_r() no longer reads the first line of an empty file.
  code_check previously recorded empty files as errored.

Tests
- New tests for all of the above.
- Existing tests: restore the real zip_peek() after tests that replace
  it; give new download tests their own repository names; add an
  renv.lock to the code_check green-light test (required since 9285b1f).
recent_commits.author: Lakens

recent_commits.message: Convert Grobid TEI to bibr export schema 12.0
recent_commits.body:
grobid_to_bibr(schema_version = "12.0") converts Grobid TEI into a 12.x
paper and saves it as a 12.0 file:

- ids are 1-based positions in document order;
- xref targets come from the xml:id each <ref> points at, for bib,
  figure, table and foot references;
- each caption and footnote is one text row with no section, after the
  body and the reference list, and there are no pseudo-sections; a
  caption starts with its printed label, taken from <head> when figDesc
  leaves it out;
- the source is the PDF next to the TEI (published.pdf for
  published.pdf.tei.xml), else the TEI, so source.sha256 matches a bibr
  export of the same PDF; paper_id is the source's name without its
  extension;
- the producer is Grobid, with the version in the TEI header, and the
  converter is metacheck; completed_at is when Grobid extracted the
  content, from the same header, else the time of the conversion;
- metacheck's own warning codes start with METACHECK_.

The body sentences are made as before. Without schema_version, the
conversion is unchanged.
recent_commits.author: Jakub Werner

recent_commits.message: Write bibr export schema 12.0 with paper_write()
recent_commits.body:
paper_write(schema_version = "12.0") saves a paper read from a bibr 12.0
export as a 12.0 file. It keeps the paper's extraction block, so a bibr
export keeps bibr as its producer and bibr's completed_at, and names
metacheck as the converter: rewriting bibr's exports changes nothing but
converter. bib_match rows made by add_bib_match() are converted to the
12.0 columns, and a score that is not on the 0-1 scale is written as null
with a METACHECK_MATCH_SCORE_NOT_0_1 warning. A paper in the older format
is refused, and so is one read from a later 12.x, since its rewrite would
have to keep keys metacheck does not know. Without schema_version,
paper_write() writes what it wrote before.

The tests validate what they write against bibr's strict schema (a copy
in tests/testthat/fixtures/bibr12) when jsonvalidate, now in Suggests, is
installed.
recent_commits.author: Jakub Werner

recent_commits.message: Read bibr export schema 12.x files
recent_commits.body:
.read_bibr() now sends a file with a root schema_version (bibr export
schema 11 and later) to .read_bibr12(), which reads 12.x and stops on any
other version. Files without a root schema_version read exactly as
before. Keys that a later 12.x adds are ignored.

A 12.x paper keeps metacheck's info table, made from metadata and source,
and info_match (metadata_match); the other tables keep their 12.x names
and meanings. Captions and footnotes are text rows with no section that
figure, table and the new footnote table point at with text_id; xref_id
is the row's own key and target_id the row it cites; paper$extraction
holds the export's extraction block. Degrees of freedom stay in
parentheses, as metacheck's statistics code expects.

inst/schema/paper-bibr12.json lists the optional tables and columns this
adds. paper_validate() and .paper_coerce() merge it into paper.json and
skip properties that are not tables (extraction); paper() and paper.json
are unchanged. ref_consistency, ref_miscitation and the table captions of
match_reported_output() read 12.x papers, and ref_accuracy compares the
0-1 match scores of 12.x papers with suggest_score / 100.
recent_commits.author: Jakub Werner

recent_commits.message: Fix .reproducibility_check_batch() hang from callr pipe deadlock (#420)
recent_commits.body:
callr::r_bg() was launched with its default stdout = "|" / stderr = "|",
which pipes a worker's output through a small, fixed-size OS buffer.
Nothing in the polling loop drains those pipes while a worker is still
running, so a paper whose output exceeded the buffer before the parent
read it would block the child on its next write() forever. The process
stays alive (is_alive() == TRUE, CPU frozen rather than accumulating),
so its slot in `running` never frees, the queue never advances past it,
and the dispatcher hangs indefinitely with the remaining queued papers
never launched.

Redirect each worker's stdout/stderr to temp files instead, tracked in
new out_files/err_files lists keyed by pid (the callr process object is
a locked R6 environment and rejects new fields directly). The failure
path now reads the stderr file instead of p$read_all_error(), and both
temp files are removed once a worker's result has been collected.

Verified against a real Docker run (workers = 2, 3 papers): all papers
launch, finish, and combine correctly.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
recent_commits.author: Daniel Lakens

recent_commits.message: Fix capture_module_tables() saving modules unnamed (#419)
recent_commits.body:
collect_module_tables() looked up saved modules by name
(j$modules[[module]]), but capture_module_tables() never named the
outputs list, so the lookup always missed and the function silently
returned an empty data frame for every paper. .load_module_tables()
had the same problem via names(saved$modules).

Name outputs from each module's own $module field (read before it is
stripped as plumbing), with a positional fallback for any NA/blank/
duplicate name. Also warn in collect_module_tables() when files exist
but none matched, instead of silently returning empty.

recent_commits.body:
DataONE: added data.piscoweb.org (PISCO, UC Santa Barbara) as a known
member node, and fixed .dataone_pid() not recognising a bare DOI whose
suffix itself contains a further slash (PISCO's own 10.6085/AA/<id>
shape). Both found via a real paper citing this DOI with no host
domain in the URL at all, which dataone_links() could not resolve at
all before this fix.

Figshare: added 28 more institutional instances (found via DataCite's
client registry, searched for "figshare" in the client name) and
Monash University's bridges.monash.edu (found separately, via a real
paper citation, since its DataCite client is named "Monash University"
rather than mentioning Figshare). Taught .figshare_id()/figshare_links()
to recognise each instance's own DOI prefix (e.g. 10.26180 for Monash,
10.25375 for ZivaHub/UCT) when cited as a bare DOI with no host domain
in the URL -- previously only the generic 10.6084/m9.figshare.* DOI
shape was recognised this way, silently missing every institutional
instance's own prefix regardless of how many hosts were already in
.figshare_vanity_hosts(). Also anchored the new id-extraction pattern
on a non-digit boundary rather than end-of-string, since a trailing
sentence period from ordinary prose ("...19095317.v1.") is a common
real-extraction artifact that end-of-string anchoring silently missed.

Every added host confirmed live to answer Figshare's own single-page-app
shell (HTTP 202, non-JSON body) rather than a real API response, the
same discipline the existing 16 vanity hosts use; several DataCite-listed
candidates were checked and excluded because their real platform is
something else entirely (DataverseNO, DTU's Orbit repository, University
of Salford's Worktribe platform).

_new_commits.message: Add Tier-1 extension rules for GIS, phylogenetics, mass spec, and 3D scan data
_new_commits.body:
data_classify_files() had no format-locked rule for ESRI Shapefile
components, GeoPackage, phylogenetic tree formats, mass spectrometry
data, 3D scan data, or generic tabular text, so recognition depended
entirely on folder/filename-keyword fallback. A file with no such hint
(e.g. sitting at an archive's root) fell through to "unknown" even
when the extension alone is unambiguous evidence of research data.

Added .shp/.dbf/.shx/.prj/.sbn/.sbx/.cpg/.gpkg, .nex/.nwk/.tre/.phy,
.mzxml/.mztab, .ply, and .tab/.table as Tier-1 data extensions, and
wired .tab/.table into data_read_head()'s delimited-text reader so the
readable=TRUE flag has a matching parser. .stl is deliberately left
alone (stays "materials"), since it conventionally names a
3D-printable model rather than scan data, unlike .ply.

Fixes #441

recent_commits.message: Test DEBIT's exact formula analytically and show its basis
recent_commits.body:
* `"exact"` now takes the range of `k` from `sum_range()` and checks the
SD bounds against `k * (n - k)` in whole-number arithmetic, folding `k`
onto the half where that product rises. This replaces a list of every
candidate `k`, so a row costs the same for any `n` (2e7 went from 1.3 s
to 0.01 s). The `"mean_n"` test moves into its own helper, unchanged.
* `debit_map()` returns `sum_lower` and `sum_upper`, the range of `k`,
which the old `x_lower` / `x_upper` columns could not explain.
* `debit_plot()` marks the attainable means `k / n` on the line, and the
vignette no longer says that a box crossing the line is enough.
* With more than 10,000 attainable means, `debit_plot()` draws only the
first mark in each cell of a 2000 x 2000 grid over the panel, found from
where the line crosses the grid lines, and says so. The plot looks the
same; `n = 2e7` went from ~14 million marks to ~10,000.
* `debit_plot()` errors if `data` has the DEBIT class but no recorded
`formula`. Class and attribute survive the same verbs, so such data were
built by hand, and guessing `"exact"` could draw marks that don't match
the verdicts.
* test-debit.R has an exhaustive oracle behind `run_full_debit_oracle`,
covering every rounding method with and without `symmetric`. It detects
exact ties itself, since `base::round()` misjudges them under `"even"`.

recent_commits.message: Make DEBIT exact for attainable means
recent_commits.body:
* The mean of `n` binary values is `k / n`, but DEBIT treated it as
continuous and accepted SDs no binary sample can have, e.g.
`debit(0.05, 0.21, 20, 2, 2)`. `formula` now takes `"exact"`, the new
default, which only tests means of that form, or `"mean_n"`, its former
only value, which keeps the previous test.
* `reconstruct_sd()` is gone: DEBIT was its only user and only ever
needed `sd_binary_mean_n()`.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Turn repeated reassignments into pipe chains with `call_on()`
recent_commits.body:
* A variable assigned two or three times in a row, each time from its
  previous value, is now one pipe chain. `call_on()` covers the steps
  that are a subset or a lambda, e.g. `call_on(\(x) x[!is.na(x)])`,
  which also stops a vector from having to be named twice to filter it.

* `head(-1L)` replaces the `x[-length(x)]` slice that started a chain in
  `write_doc_audit_total_n()`.

* `check_lengths_congruent()` and the manufactured function body in
  `function_map_seq()` are left as they are.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Remove remnants of string key values
recent_commits.body:
* `grim_plot(show_data = FALSE)` built its dummy data from `x = "0.00"`,
  so its default decimal count came from counting characters. It now
  uses `x = 0` and a `digits_x` column, like mapper output.
* `*_map_seq()` no longer guesses a missing `digits_*` column with
  `decimal_places()` on numeric values, which lose trailing zeros.
* `index_case_from_diff()` drops its branch for string sequences, which
  no mapper produces anymore.
* Drop `as.numeric()` calls and `x_orig` copies on key values that
  `check_newly_numeric()` has already required to be numeric.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Reject a string `x` in `grim_total()` and `grim_probability()`
recent_commits.body:
* They coerced `x` with `as.numeric()`, so `grim_total("5.19", 20, 2)`
  returned a count where `grim()` rejects the same string. A missing `x`
  still gives `NA`.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Start pipe chains in the tests with the object
recent_commits.body:
* Tests written since c3abc01 had fallen back to `f1(x) |> f2()` and
  nested `expect_*(f(x))` calls. They now follow that commit's model:
  `x |> f1() |> f2()`, with the expectation at the end of the chain and
  the pipes of parallel lines aligned.

* Only a compound first argument such as `list()`, `c()`, or
  `tibble::tibble()` still starts a chain as a call. `expect_snapshot()`
  code is unchanged.

* Extracting from a call's result is a step of the chain:
  `purrr::pluck()` for names and positions, `head()` for slices.

* Add the internal `call_on()` for steps that are an operator or an
  anonymous function, e.g. `call_on(\(x) x %% 1 == 0)`. It also covers
  `formals(f)$name`, since `purrr::pluck()` rejects pairlists.

* The suite passes with the same 19,570 expectations as before.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Record call settings in one attribute, not in flag classes
recent_commits.body:
* Classes on scrutiny output are now for S3 dispatch only. Settings that
functions downstream need live in a single list attribute, "scrutiny",
read with the internal `scrutiny_meta()`.

* Basic mappers record every argument that applied to the whole call,
defaults resolved, as `args`. This replaces the "scrutiny_rounding_*"
and "scrutiny_percent_true" classes and makes `function_map()`'s
unreleased `.name_class_flags` argument unnecessary, so it is removed.

* Sequence mappers carry over the initial `fun()` call's record and add
`fun_args`, `name_key_result`, and `dispersion_linear`, replacing two
attributes and the "scrutiny_map_seq_disp_nonlinear" class. The
"scrutiny_seq_df" and "scrutiny_seq_test" classes became `seq_df` and
`seq_test` elements.

* This removes the regex parsing of class strings in `grim_plot()` and
`audit_seq()`, and the class rewrite in `function_map_seq()`. New tests
cover the recorded arguments, the sequence-test check, and the
rejection of non-linear dispersion.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Correct stale documentation found in the dead-weight audit
recent_commits.body:
* `disperse()`: `n_change` is an integer step count, not string labels.
* `decimal_places_scalar()` is about 1.8x faster, not "much faster".
* `row_to_colnames()` keeps the class of a data frame; only a matrix
  becomes a tibble.
* The in-depth vignette no longer advises counting decimal places in a
  single-case function; since 0.6, tests take `digits_*` instead.
* NEWS no longer says vectorized `rounding` etc. take an old path in
  `reround()`, which requires them to have length 1.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Explain missing bounds columns in `debit_plot()`
recent_commits.body:
* `debit_map(show_rec = FALSE) |> debit_plot()` failed with a raw vctrs
  subsetting error. It now names the missing columns and points to
  `show_rec = TRUE`.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Add the `.name_class` class in `function_map_seq()`
recent_commits.body:
* It was passed into the dots of `function_map_seq_proto()`, which ignores
  them, so the documented class never reached the output.
  `function_map_total_n()` always added it; the seq factory now does the
  same.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Name the separators in `split_by_parens()` warnings for any `sep`
recent_commits.body:
* `message_sep_if_cols_excluded()` only knew the keywords and length-2
  vectors, so `sep = "("` left the warning ending in "elements, .". It now
  translates `sep` first, like the splitting itself does.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Select all-`NA` and comma columns in the `*_df()` wrappers
recent_commits.body:
* `restore_zeros_df()` and `decimal_places_df()` failed on an all-`NA`
  column, where `is_numeric_like()` is `NA` and `where()` needs a flag.
  A new internal `is_numeric_like_col()` treats such a column as
  numeric-like and reads comma decimals with `sep_in` / `sep`, which were
  silently skipped before.
* `restore_zeros_df()`'s `sep_out` defaults to `sep_in`, as documented.
* `decimal_places_df()` only warns about columns `cols` selected, and both
  functions' warnings say what happens under `check_numeric_like = FALSE`.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Evaluate `seq_disperse_df()`'s dots in the caller's frame
recent_commits.body:
* The dots were captured with `rlang::enexprs()` and evaluated inside the
  function, so a variable local to the caller was not found. They are now
  passed on to `tibble::tibble()` as they are.
* The `track_diff_var` docs said `seq_disperse()` ignores it; it makes the
  function return a list.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Put the changelog link inside the missing-digits error
recent_commits.body:
* `error_digits_missing()` printed the link with `on.exit()`, apart
  from the error, so it leaked into the test output wherever the error
  was expected.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Keep `audit()` summary columns double when all values are `NA`
recent_commits.body:
* 40e4e9d's `on_non_na()` returned a logical `NA` for an all-missing
  column, so `mean`, `sd`, `median`, `min`, and `max` became logical
  when every selected column was missing.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Read a factor by its labels in `rounding_bias()`
recent_commits.body:
* d0f1c3b converted `x` with `as.numeric()`, which turns a factor into
  its level codes, so a factor gave a bias of zero without complaint.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Trim Unicode spaces before counting decimal places
recent_commits.body:
* d0f1c3b replaced `stringr::str_trim()` with an ASCII-only trim, so a
  trailing no-break space hid an exponent: `decimal_places("1.5e3\u00a0")`
  was 1 instead of 0.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Write out unusual number spellings in `restore_zeros()`
recent_commits.body:
* d0f1c3b made `restore_zeros()` append zeros to the input text rather
  than reformat it, so spellings like `".5"`, `"+1.5"`, and `"0x1A"`
  came back padded but otherwise untouched.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Read any escaped separator as the character itself
recent_commits.body:
* d0f1c3b made `sep` and `sep_in` literal, keeping only the old default
  `"\\."` as a regex. Other escaped separators such as `"\\,"` were
  then not found, and `decimal_places()` silently counted 0.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Bring docs and NEWS in line with the code
recent_commits.body:
* rounding-in-depth.Rmd and NEWS still described the old
  `round_down_from()` threshold (26ab044).
* `?grim_plot` didn't mention that `percent = TRUE` adds 2 decimal
  places (b8fc076).
* The seq mappers documented the old `out_min`/`out_max` defaults
  (4ac58f7).
* NEWS described a fix to DEBIT tiles that no longer exist, and
  overstated the `is_seq_dispersed()` fix.
* The missing-digits error suggested a DEBIT call with `x = 1.4`,
  which itself fails.
* A data-raw comment pointed to a moved file.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Divide each branch by its own denominator in `reround_to_fraction()`
recent_commits.body:
* A compound method returns two values per input value, interleaved, but
  `reround_to_fraction()` and `reround_to_fraction_level()` recycled a
  vector `denominator` over them unpaired.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Read key arguments passed through dots in `absorb_key_args()`
recent_commits.body:
* dbef5d1 captured only key arguments that are formals of the caller, so
  a handwritten function forwarding them through `...` no longer had its
  columns renamed.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Reject a `consistency` column under a custom `.name_key_result`
recent_commits.body:
* 9345d97 made the check look for `.name_key_result` only, but
  `function_map()` builds the result as `consistency` before renaming
  it, so a user's column of that name was silently dropped. Check both
  names again.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Run `debit_plot()` examples only where ggrepel is installed
recent_commits.body:
* 981ce94 moved ggrepel to Suggests, but the example, the vignette
  chunk, and the tests still called `debit_plot()` with its default
  `show_labels = TRUE`, which needs it.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Reconstruct 0-row `*_map_total_n()` output without failing
recent_commits.body:
* dcb7d82 let the total-n mappers return 0 rows when no pair of group
  sizes is left, but `reverse_map_total_n()` and `audit_total_n()` then
  failed on it with "wrong sign in 'by' argument".
* The reported columns of that output also came out logical.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Clip the `debit_plot()` band instead of cutting it off
recent_commits.body:
* The y-axis limits sat on the scale, which drops every ribbon row with
  an edge outside of them, so the band from 5e6fce9 showed only as
  slivers. Put the limits on the coordinate system instead.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Take `incons_to_prob` over the decidable cases only
recent_commits.body:
* Since c0904ba, the mean probability skipped undecidable rows while the
  inconsistency rate still counted them, so each such row pulled the
  ratio towards zero.
* Correct the NEWS claim that `audit_cols_minimal()` excluded those rows.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Keep `items` apart from `n` in `*_map_total_n()` output
recent_commits.body:
* The total-n tier returned `n * items`, so `reverse_map_total_n()` and
  `audit_total_n()` reported that product as the total. Undo the merge
  as the seq tier does.
* `grim_plot()` now multiplies an `items` column back into `n`, which
  the seq tier's output needed as well.
recent_commits.author: Lukas Jung

recent_commits.message: Let GRIMMER check wide sum-of-squares ranges in chunks
recent_commits.body:
* The enumeration limit from 3b7248a also applied to the sums of
  squares, whose range grows with the SD, not just `n`. A large SD
  reported with few decimals was refused at `n = 20`.
* Walk that range in chunks instead, and keep the limit only for the
  candidate sums.

Free, open-source AI academic paper reviewer that outperforms popular paid AI reviewers.

You provide your own API key and pay the LLM provider directly — typically **under $2 per review**.

Don't want to run it locally? Use the [web interface](https://coarse.ink/) instead.


Get an API key from [OpenRouter](https://openrouter.ai/keys) (free to sign up), then:

```bash
uvx coarse-ink review paper.pdf --api-key sk-or-v1-YOUR_KEY
```

That's it. The review is written to `paper_review.md` in the current directory.


coarse requires Python 3.12+. If you don't have `uvx`, install [uv](https://docs.

highlights.message: Widen archive-member byte-range retry beyond the fixed 403/429/5xx list (#429)
highlights.body:
.http_range_bytes() -- the call .zip_member_fetch() makes for both a
member's local header and its compressed data -- only retried a response
matching .storage_is_transient()'s fixed list (403, 429, 500, 502, 503,
504). Any other status (a plain 401, a 400, or anything else not on that
list) was accepted as final after exactly one try, even when the identical
request succeeded moments later on manual reproduction: nothing
distinguishes "this host will never honour ranges" from "that one request
happened to fail" for an unlisted status.

.range_status_is_transient() now retries anything except 200 (host is
deliberately ignoring Range -- a fixed property of the host/URL a retry
cannot change) and 206 (success). Verified against a real, unmocked local
HTTP server that returns 401 once then 206 -- httr2's own retry loop
(req_perform1 -> retry_is_transient(), independent of req_error()'s is_error
override) correctly retries and succeeds on the second attempt.

httr2::local_mocked_responses()/with_mocked_responses() do not exercise
req_retry()'s actual retry loop at all (mock responses return through
handle_resp() before the while(tries < max_tries) loop is reached) -- a
limitation already independently documented elsewhere in this codebase
(test-repo-download.R's skipped "skip_on_api_limit = TRUE gives up on a
confirmed rate limit fast" test). Tests here check the request's configured
retry policy directly instead of trying to simulate multiple attempts
through a mock.

highlights.message: Test DEBIT's exact formula analytically and show its basis
highlights.body:
* `"exact"` now takes the range of `k` from `sum_range()` and checks the
SD bounds against `k * (n - k)` in whole-number arithmetic, folding `k`
onto the half where that product rises. This replaces a list of every
candidate `k`, so a row costs the same for any `n` (2e7 went from 1.3 s
to 0.01 s). The `"mean_n"` test moves into its own helper, unchanged.
* `debit_map()` returns `sum_lower` and `sum_upper`, the range of `k`,
which the old `x_lower` / `x_upper` columns could not explain.
* `debit_plot()` marks the attainable means `k / n` on the line, and the
vignette no longer says that a box crossing the line is enough.
* With more than 10,000 attainable means, `debit_plot()` draws only the
first mark in each cell of a 2000 x 2000 grid over the panel, found from
where the line crosses the grid lines, and says so. The plot looks the
same; `n = 2e7` went from ~14 million marks to ~10,000.
* `debit_plot()` errors if `data` has the DEBIT class but no recorded
`formula`. Class and attribute survive the same verbs, so such data were
built by hand, and guessing `"exact"` could draw marks that don't match
the verdicts.
* test-debit.R has an exhaustive oracle behind `run_full_debit_oracle`,
covering every rounding method with and without `symmetric`. It detects
exact ties itself, since `base::round()` misjudges them under `"even"`.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Make DEBIT exact for attainable means
highlights.body:
* The mean of `n` binary values is `k / n`, but DEBIT treated it as
continuous and accepted SDs no binary sample can have, e.g.
`debit(0.05, 0.21, 20, 2, 2)`. `formula` now takes `"exact"`, the new
default, which only tests means of that form, or `"mean_n"`, its former
only value, which keeps the previous test.
* `reconstruct_sd()` is gone: DEBIT was its only user and only ever
needed `sd_binary_mean_n()`.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Turn repeated reassignments into pipe chains with `call_on()`
highlights.body:
* A variable assigned two or three times in a row, each time from its
  previous value, is now one pipe chain. `call_on()` covers the steps
  that are a subset or a lambda, e.g. `call_on(\(x) x[!is.na(x)])`,
  which also stops a vector from having to be named twice to filter it.

* `head(-1L)` replaces the `x[-length(x)]` slice that started a chain in
  `write_doc_audit_total_n()`.

* `check_lengths_congruent()` and the manufactured function body in
  `function_map_seq()` are left as they are.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Remove remnants of string key values
highlights.body:
* `grim_plot(show_data = FALSE)` built its dummy data from `x = "0.00"`,
  so its default decimal count came from counting characters. It now
  uses `x = 0` and a `digits_x` column, like mapper output.
* `*_map_seq()` no longer guesses a missing `digits_*` column with
  `decimal_places()` on numeric values, which lose trailing zeros.
* `index_case_from_diff()` drops its branch for string sequences, which
  no mapper produces anymore.
* Drop `as.numeric()` calls and `x_orig` copies on key values that
  `check_newly_numeric()` has already required to be numeric.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Reject a string `x` in `grim_total()` and `grim_probability()`
highlights.body:
* They coerced `x` with `as.numeric()`, so `grim_total("5.19", 20, 2)`
  returned a count where `grim()` rejects the same string. A missing `x`
  still gives `NA`.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Start pipe chains in the tests with the object
highlights.body:
* Tests written since c3abc01 had fallen back to `f1(x) |> f2()` and
  nested `expect_*(f(x))` calls. They now follow that commit's model:
  `x |> f1() |> f2()`, with the expectation at the end of the chain and
  the pipes of parallel lines aligned.

* Only a compound first argument such as `list()`, `c()`, or
  `tibble::tibble()` still starts a chain as a call. `expect_snapshot()`
  code is unchanged.

* Extracting from a call's result is a step of the chain:
  `purrr::pluck()` for names and positions, `head()` for slices.

* Add the internal `call_on()` for steps that are an operator or an
  anonymous function, e.g. `call_on(\(x) x %% 1 == 0)`. It also covers
  `formals(f)$name`, since `purrr::pluck()` rejects pairlists.

* The suite passes with the same 19,570 expectations as before.

highlights.message: Record archive-member download failures in download_repo_files() itself (#429)
highlights.body:
The previous commit fixed error propagation inside .zip_fetch_members()/
.zip_member_fetch(), but missed the actual call site the issue reported:
download_repo_files()'s archive-member block (R/repo-download.R) wraps
.zip_fetch_members() in tryCatch(..., error = function(e) NULL) and, on

individual member coming back ok = FALSE -- just does `next`, leaving
file_location = NA with nothing recorded anywhere. This is the exact code
quoted in the issue.

Moved `failed`'s initialization earlier (it previously appeared after this
block ran, so there was nowhere to record into) and now populate it for
all three failure shapes, matching the has_url path's existing convention:
the roll-up message() and attr(files, "failed") already downstream pick

highlights.message: Record why a zip archive-member fetch failed instead of a silent NULL (#429)
highlights.body:
.zip_fetch_members()/.zip_member_fetch() collapsed every failure -- a
transient range-request error, a corrupt local header, a CRC mismatch, a
path-traversal rejection, a write failure -- into an indistinguishable
ok = FALSE with no message anywhere, so a corpus-scale run had no way to
tell a retryable failure apart from a host that will never support this.
Each failure path now records a one-line reason, and the five per-provider
download functions (Dryad, Zenodo, Figshare, Dataverse, ReShare) surface it
as a progress message and attach it as a `failed` attribute on the returned
table, matching the convention download_repo_files() already uses.

highlights.body:
* `restore_zeros_df()` and `decimal_places_df()` failed on an all-`NA`
  column, where `is_numeric_like()` is `NA` and `where()` needs a flag.
  A new internal `is_numeric_like_col()` treats such a column as
  numeric-like and reads comma decimals with `sep_in` / `sep`, which were
  silently skipped before.
* `restore_zeros_df()`'s `sep_out` defaults to `sep_in`, as documented.
* `decimal_places_df()` only warns about columns `cols` selected, and both
  functions' warnings say what happens under `check_numeric_like = FALSE`.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Evaluate `seq_disperse_df()`'s dots in the caller's frame
highlights.body:
* The dots were captured with `rlang::enexprs()` and evaluated inside the
  function, so a variable local to the caller was not found. They are now
  passed on to `tibble::tibble()` as they are.
* The `track_diff_var` docs said `seq_disperse()` ignores it; it makes the
  function return a list.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Put the changelog link inside the missing-digits error
highlights.body:
* `error_digits_missing()` printed the link with `on.exit()`, apart
  from the error, so it leaked into the test output wherever the error
  was expected.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Keep `audit()` summary columns double when all values are `NA`
highlights.body:
* 40e4e9d's `on_non_na()` returned a logical `NA` for an all-missing
  column, so `mean`, `sd`, `median`, `min`, and `max` became logical
  when every selected column was missing.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Read a factor by its labels in `rounding_bias()`
highlights.body:
* d0f1c3b converted `x` with `as.numeric()`, which turns a factor into
  its level codes, so a factor gave a bias of zero without complaint.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Trim Unicode spaces before counting decimal places
highlights.body:
* d0f1c3b replaced `stringr::str_trim()` with an ASCII-only trim, so a
  trailing no-break space hid an exponent: `decimal_places("1.5e3\u00a0")`
  was 1 instead of 0.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Write out unusual number spellings in `restore_zeros()`
highlights.body:
* d0f1c3b made `restore_zeros()` append zeros to the input text rather
  than reformat it, so spellings like `".5"`, `"+1.5"`, and `"0x1A"`
  came back padded but otherwise untouched.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Read any escaped separator as the character itself
highlights.body:
* d0f1c3b made `sep` and `sep_in` literal, keeping only the old default
  `"\\."` as a regex. Other escaped separators such as `"\\,"` were
  then not found, and `decimal_places()` silently counted 0.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Bring docs and NEWS in line with the code
highlights.body:
* rounding-in-depth.Rmd and NEWS still described the old
  `round_down_from()` threshold (26ab044).
* `?grim_plot` didn't mention that `percent = TRUE` adds 2 decimal
  places (b8fc076).
* The seq mappers documented the old `out_min`/`out_max` defaults
  (4ac58f7).
* NEWS described a fix to DEBIT tiles that no longer exist, and
  overstated the `is_seq_dispersed()` fix.
* The missing-digits error suggested a DEBIT call with `x = 1.4`,
  which itself fails.
* A data-raw comment pointed to a moved file.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Divide each branch by its own denominator in `reround_to_fraction()`
highlights.body:
* A compound method returns two values per input value, interleaved, but
  `reround_to_fraction()` and `reround_to_fraction_level()` recycled a
  vector `denominator` over them unpaired.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Read key arguments passed through dots in `absorb_key_args()`
highlights.body:
* dbef5d1 captured only key arguments that are formals of the caller, so
  a handwritten function forwarding them through `...` no longer had its
  columns renamed.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Reject a `consistency` column under a custom `.name_key_result`
highlights.body:
* 9345d97 made the check look for `.name_key_result` only, but
  `function_map()` builds the result as `consistency` before renaming
  it, so a user's column of that name was silently dropped. Check both
  names again.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Run `debit_plot()` examples only where ggrepel is installed
highlights.body:
* 981ce94 moved ggrepel to Suggests, but the example, the vignette
  chunk, and the tests still called `debit_plot()` with its default
  `show_labels = TRUE`, which needs it.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Reconstruct 0-row `*_map_total_n()` output without failing
highlights.body:
* dcb7d82 let the total-n mappers return 0 rows when no pair of group
  sizes is left, but `reverse_map_total_n()` and `audit_total_n()` then
  failed on it with "wrong sign in 'by' argument".
* The reported columns of that output also came out logical.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Clip the `debit_plot()` band instead of cutting it off
highlights.body:
* The y-axis limits sat on the scale, which drops every ribbon row with
  an edge outside of them, so the band from 5e6fce9 showed only as
  slivers. Put the limits on the coordinate system instead.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Take `incons_to_prob` over the decidable cases only
highlights.body:
* Since c0904ba, the mean probability skipped undecidable rows while the
  inconsistency rate still counted them, so each such row pulled the
  ratio towards zero.
* Correct the NEWS claim that `audit_cols_minimal()` excluded those rows.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung

highlights.message: Keep `items` apart from `n` in `*_map_total_n()` output
highlights.body:
* The total-n tier returned `n * items`, so `reverse_map_total_n()` and
  `audit_total_n()` reported that product as the total. Undo the merge
  as the seq tier does.
* `grim_plot()` now multiplies an `items` column back into `n`, which
  the seq tier's output needed as well.
highlights.author: Lukas Jung
